messages:
customer-jdoe: Hey team — since ~09:10 UTC we've been getting a ton of 5xx/504s from /v1/generate on hosted. 20-30% of requests failing, tail latency huge. Example: curl returned 504 with X-Request-ID: rwd-8f3b2c. We're on region eu-west-1, model=redwood-13b-v2, plan=standard. Can you look? Our feature is user-facing and is degrading.
sam.support: Thanks — looking. Can you paste a failed request id and approximate timestamp? Also, are you doing long context lengths or high concurrency bursts right now?
customer-jdoe: Request id rwd-8f3b2c at 2026-03-15T09:12:06Z. Concurrency spiked to ~250 req/s after a marketing email. Most requests are short (<=512 tokens) but lots of small ones.
maya.engineer: grabbing logs for that request id... seeing gateway timeout at the edge: 504 Gateway Timeout from gw-api-01, but downstream logs from inference-runtime show: "enqueue failed: queue_full after 200ms (max_queue_wait_ms=200)" for model redwood-13b-v2.
emma.sre: Metrics snapshot: continuous_batching.backlog_count > 4000 for the model, queue_depth configured 1024, 95th percentile queue wait ~220ms. tail latency elevated for tokens: token_emit_latency_p90 jumped from 60ms to 520ms. This looks like queue saturation causing enqueue timeouts and then gateway 504s.
raj.oncall: Paging eng-runtime. This looks like a classic batching backlog/queue-depth limit hit during a traffic spike. Immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily reduce batching window and max batch size for redwood-13b-v2, 2) enable fallback routing to smaller model (redwood-7b-v1) for non-critical requests, 3) emergency scale-up of worker pool for that model. Which can we do fastest in hosted?
maya.engineer: We can flip routing to fallback in ~2-3 mins (config toggle). Reducing batching window also quick (runtime config push). Autoscale will take ~5-10 mins to spin up more GPUs in eu-west-1; we should do config changes first.
sam.support: I'll ask customer if they can accept degraded quality/fallback to 7b for the next hour while we stabilize.
customer-jdoe: OK to fallback to 7b for web-tier only, not for our background critical jobs. Web-tier traffic is ~80% of the spike.
raj.oncall: Plan: A) set routing rule for model redwood-13b-v2 to overflow to redwood-7b-v1 for route:web-client. B) reduce continuous_batching.window_ms from 100 to 20 for redwood-13b-v2. C) set max_queue_wait_ms to 500 -> 300 to avoid long tails. D) trigger emergency autoscale + monitor for errors. Emma, can you run the dashboard queries to baseline?
emma.sre: Running queries: increase in enqueue_rate at 09:10, errors_at_edge (504) aligns with enqueue_failed logs. Will push dashboard with these widgets: queue_depth, backlog_count, enqueue_wait_p95, model_worker_count.
infra-bot: ACTION: config-change(redwood.routing) initiated by maya.engineer at 2026-03-15T09:18:12Z
maya.engineer: Pushed routing rule: route:web-client now has fallback redwood-7b-v1 with 100% overflow. Reducing batching window now.
maya.engineer: Pushed continuous_batching.window_ms=20 for redwood-13b-v2; pushed max_batch_size=16 -> 8. Watch for throughput drop.
customer-jdoe: Seeing errors drop immediately from 25% -> ~6% for web-tier. Background jobs still showing some 504s, but much better overall.
raj.oncall: Starting autoscale of runtime pool for redwood-13b-v2 in eu-west-1 (requested +4 workers). ETA ~7 minutes.
emma.sre: Monitoring: backlog_count halved in 2 minutes, enqueue_wait_p95 down to 80ms. Tail 99th token latency still high but trending down.
maya.engineer: Found a small leak: one worker node stuck at high GPU memory usage causing slow KV cache eviction; restarting that worker cleared several stuck batches. Log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:45Z] worker-37: kv-cache-evict loop blocked, mem > 95%, preserving in-flight slots
[2026-03-15T09:15:02Z] worker-37: restart initiated by maya.engineer
```
sam.support: Noting customer impact and refund eligibility. Customer wants a short postmortem after stabilization.
customer-jdoe: Appreciate the quick response. Two asks: 1) can you prevent this for future scheduled marketing bursts? 2) can you share temporary credits for the downtime?
raj.oncall: Action items: - eng-runtime to add adaptive overflow policy for high-traffic spikes (owner: maya.engineer) - add safeguard to auto-fallback to smaller models when queue_depth > 800 (owner: eng-prod) - support to issue credits (owner: sam.support) - run load-test to repro pattern (owner: eng-sre).
maya.engineer: Noted. I'll open a runtime PR to add dynamic batching window adjustment and a soft overflow path that starts at queue_depth > 600. Will also add a runbook step: if enqueue_failed rate > 1% => reduce batching window and flip fallback.
emma.sre: Autoscale completed at 09:25, worker_count +4. Post-mitigation metrics: overall 5xxs back to normal baseline, p95 latency ~95ms. I'll keep the dashboard pinned.
infra-bot: INCIDENT: incident-20260315-002 created by raj.oncall at 2026-03-15T09:20:05Z, severity=P1
sam.support: I spoke with customer — they've accepted fallback for the web-tier; asking for credits. I've created support ticket SUP-4421 and linked the incident.
customer-jdoe: Service is smooth now, thanks. Please do the postmortem and let me know when safeguards are in place.
maya.engineer: Will draft a short postmortem and link to incident-20260315-002. Preliminary root cause: sudden traffic spike + one degraded worker + batching window+queue config that allowed long tails; combined to saturate enqueue pipeline. Fixes: worker health checks, dynamic batching window, overflow policy, fallback routing.
raj.oncall: Closing loop: if anyone sees re-occurrence ping me. Good job on quick mitigation.
sam.support: Closing customer loop and issuing credits now. Will attach postmortem when ready.
customer-jdoe: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
